passage.label: Horn blown one blast earth mountains lifted leveled one blow Day Resurrection occur heaven split infirm angels edges bear Throne Lord above them eight; Day exhibited judgement nothing concealed hidden; given record right hand says here read record certain meeting account pleasant life elevated garden fruit picked hanging near eat drink satisfaction put forth days past; given record left hand says wish not given record not known account wish death decisive wealth not availed gone authority; seize shackle Hellfire drive chain seventy cubits insert; not believe Allah Most Great nor encourage feeding poor; no devoted friend this Day no food except discharge wounds none eat except sinners

arabicExcerpts.text: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفۡخَةٞ وَٰحِدَةٞ
وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ
وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذٖ ثَمَٰنِيَةٞ
يَوۡمَئِذٖ تُعۡرَضُونَ لَا تَخۡفَىٰ مِنكُمۡ خَافِيَةٞ
فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَآ أَسۡلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَيَّامِ ٱلۡخَالِيَةِ
وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
ثُمَّ فِي سِلۡسِلَةٖ ذَرۡعُهَا سَبۡعُونَ ذِرَاعٗا فَٱسۡلُكُوهُ
إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ

mainSubject.label: The single Horn blast lifting and levelling earth and mountains so the Resurrection occurs, heaven splitting in infirmity with angels at its edges and eight bearing the Throne above them; all exhibited for judgement with nothing concealed; the right-hand record-holder inviting others to read it because he was certain of meeting his account, entering a pleasant life in an elevated garden with near-hanging fruit and satisfied eating for past deeds; the left-hand record-holder wishing he had never received it nor known his account, wishing death decisive since wealth and authority failed him; the command to seize, shackle, drive into Hellfire and insert into a seventy-cubit chain because he neither believed in Allah the Most Great nor encouraged feeding the poor, leaving him without devoted friend and with only wound-discharge food eaten by sinners

subordinateSubjects.label: The Horn blown with a single blast
Earth and mountains lifted and levelled with one blow
The Resurrection occurring on that Day
The heaven splitting open, infirm on that Day
Angels at its edges with eight bearing the Throne of the Lord above them
All exhibited for judgement with nothing concealed remaining hidden
The right-hand record-holder inviting others to read his record
His certainty of meeting his account declared as the reason
A pleasant life granted to him
An elevated garden named as his pleasant-life setting
Its fruit hanging near for picking
Eating and drinking in satisfaction for what was put forth in past days
The left-hand record-holder wishing he had never been given his record
Wishing he had not known his account
Wishing his death had been the decisive end
His wealth declared to have availed him nothing
His authority declared gone from him
The command to seize him and shackle him
Then to drive him into Hellfire
Then to insert him into a chain seventy cubits long
The cause named: he did not believe in Allah the Most Great
Nor did he encourage the feeding of the poor
No devoted friend available to him on that Day
No food for him except the discharge of wounds
None eating that food except the sinners

commandsAndProhibitions.description: Seize him and shackle him — the divine verdict on the left-hand record-holder.

notes: Wave 10 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the flood-reminder and conscious-ear statement (12) before the Horn blast opens (13); P2 ends with the wound-discharge food verdict (37) before the seen-unseen oath begins (38); P3 runs through the Messenger-word affirmation, the poet-soothsayer denials and the fabrication counterfactual (38-47); P4 covers the reminder-for-the-righteous, the regret declaration, the truth-of-certainty and the closing exaltation (48-52).
